text_fidelity_a:
Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise) This is the second case I have gotten that I could not give a good rating because of the bottom part, which does not fit with the adapter (to allow older devices to work with the new iPhone), and it does not fit most professional cables that go into the headphone jack.
Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise)

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show 5 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- Smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Charcoal (I have upgraded my review again to take off another star. This gadget is IMPOSSIBLE. You have to BELLOW at it to make it do anything. I am sorry I bought it, and the second one that we sent to my mother-in-law so we could talk face to face. Unfortunately, no one where she lived knew how to set it up and she died before we could set it up for her. So I basically wasted $145 for two Echo Shows because the one we have at home is no prize.)

(I have upgraded my review to take off a star. Since we have not been able to do face-to-face calling on it--no one where my MIL lives knows how to set it up--it basically is useless for the purpose we got it. Yeah, I loaded some photos on it so now I can look up and see our previous dog or a pic of my mom. But really, the old 2nd Generation Echo Dot responded better and more quickly. THIS THING IS DEAF. I used to be able to call up the stairs before I took the dog out "Echo, what's the temperature outside?" and like THAT I'd get a response. You have to bellow at the Show two or three times. Sometimes I have to stand right next to it to make it listen. But it loves my husband's voice and always responds. The drop-ins were crisp and clear on the Dot. It was a real waste of money.)

We had a bright idea: buy one of these for us, and buy one for my husband's mother, so we could video call her at any time (she lives 2 hours drive away), and his sister who lives in with his mom. Well, due to circumstances, we still haven't gotten the second Echo Show down to Mom, but are using the first one. Right now we are not making much use of the screen, save for a clock and a thermometer, but we have branched out into routines that are rather fun. We have tried out its video capabilities and that is very good, although we have trouble with backlighting from where our Show is placed.

I have two complaints about the Show: I think the voice is more muffled, and it doesn't seem as voice responsive as the Dot. If anything is running in the background, like the television or music, it gets really hard of hearing. We have to shout.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show 5 (1st Gen, 2019 release) -- Smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Charcoal

text_fidelity_a: Logitech Harmony One Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) In the beginning, you will love this remote. But it will break. Guaranteed. We had one stop working, and Logitech replaced it. We dropped the replacement once (just from coffee table to floor, but it's fragile!) and the screen cracked. We were upset that it broke so easily but knew it was damage not covered by warranty, so we didn't submit a claim. We figured we'd just had a freak accident/bad luck, and bought a third one. One day I picked that one up and the screen was whited out. Over the next few days, black started to seep across the screen from one edge. By the time I had to send a picture of the remote to Logitech for our warranty claim, you could see cracks at the edge. That remote was never dropped. My best guess it that I set it down on the side table as though it were a remote, not a Faberge egg. Logitech refuses to honor their warranty. It's like beating your head against a wall. Lots of "I understand you must be frustrated," and no actual help. Not acceptable for a product that costs so much. Mine is not the only review that says this -- please believe it! Unless you have the money to buy a new one every 6 months (the longest that one of our three Harmony Ones has ever lasted), just don't do it.

text_fidelity_a:
ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb Growing up I always had a radio in my room. Times are a little different now and I tend to get my music from the Internet, but there are still times when local radio stations are a better choice - particularly during power outages or when getting local news. I have had very good fortune with Sony electronics and computers in the past so I was eager to try this AM/FM tuner and had high expectations. It did not disappoint me.

Let me very clear about this unit - it is for AM/FM receiving only. It does not play MP3’s, it doesn’t play CDs and it doesn’t stream from the Internet. It’s just an AM/FM tuner. It does this quite well, though - better than most other tuners I have used in the last several years.

Right out of the box, this unit looks nostalgic. It has a classic AM/FM radio look and feel, very similar to a radio my father used to have in his workshop when I was a kid. This is a big plus for me, just for the fact that it takes me back to my childhood.

I plugged it in and turned it on, and I immediately tuned to one of the [relatively] local stations. It picked it up and played it very clearly, better than most other tuners I have used in the last 4-5 years. It is definitely better than the car’s radio. I “surfed” the dial and found other stations that I have listened to in the past but thought were out of range and this little radio did a good job of picking them up and playing with minimal static. That’s really all I could ask. It’s not a miracle radio though and it cannot pick up FM stations hundreds of miles away, but it has better range than most I have used recently.

I like that it can be used on AC power or on batteries. That will be handy during weather events.

I can’t find any real reason to complain about this tuner. It works great and looks great too. It is a little on the pricey side which is par for the course for Sony electronics, but it is a fine tuner that is worth its asking price.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICF-506 Analog Tuning Portable FM/AM Radio, Black, 2.14 lb

text_fidelity_a:
Computer Speakers for Desktop/Laptop/Mac, USB Powered PC Speaker, 2.0 Channel Stereo Multimedia Speaker for TV, Notebook, Built-in Diaphragm,3w3w Horn and in-Line Volume Control TOMOT FT-165 There's a lot I really like about these. Let me start off by pointing out, however, these are NOT USB SPEAKERS. They are simply powered off USB and use a standard headphone jack as the audio input. I have to admit, at first I was taken aback by how small they are, and assumed they must produce weak sound as a result (I'm used to a set of Harmon/Kardon speakers on my desktop which are bigger than these). But despite their size, they actually produce a really great and full sound, with an almost exaggerated stereo effect thanks to individual speakers pointing in different directions.
What I love most about it, however, is that it is USB powered. That means no additional plugs needed on my desktop, and in fact they are fantastic for boosting the audio on a laptop. In the included picture I'm posting with this, I have an old Dell Laptop that my kids use to watch things on, and these sound FAR better than the tiny built in laptop speaker. Since it is USB powered, it can be simply be run directly off the laptop itself, no additional wires or outlets necessary. Put one plug into an available USB slot, the other into the headphone jack. It makes a nice and neat looking portable setup. The thing is, I can't help but wonder why it isn't just a 100% USB sound system? I have a pair of headphones that I love using that are completely digital- it identifies as its own sound card when plugged in and requires only that one USB plug. I sort of assumed that this would be something similar to that and therefore require only that ONE plug to operate. In some cases, the digital sound systems are better than analog plug ones (interference, for example) anyway, so it seems strange to have an analog speaker system powered by a digital USB port. But I guess there can be interesting uses for this too.
For example, a device like an older phone with a headphone jack can connect to this which wouldn't work with USB. Or enhancing the speaker of an Echo Dot and powering it off a dual USB outlet (one for the Dot, the other for the speakers). It is definitely an interesting and useful thing to have around! And for the price, color me impressed!
text_fidelity_b: Computer Speakers for Desktop/Laptop/Mac, USB Powered PC Speaker, 2.0 Channel Stereo Multimedia Speaker for TV, Notebook, Built-in Diaphragm,3w3w Horn and in-Line Volume Control TOMOT FT-165

Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal) [[VIDEOID:a23b5cd930e819bd2cae7872ede2dd37]] I decided to finally upgrade my Kindle from the first Paperwhite when I found out I could get a 25% discount and a $5 Amazon gift card for trading in my very old and unused Kindle Keyboard 1st gen, as well as other bonuses of 6 months free Kindle Unlimited (approx $60) plus a 30 day Audible trial.

I’m very happy with it and it has some great features.
I do like the adjustable amber tint, but I also really like the ability to invert the colors to white print on a black background. This is even easier on the eyes, but it does have a noticeable (and irritating) white flash every few page turns when using the buttons, and almost with every page turn when advancing with the touch screen. I believe this is the e-ink refreshing. I will probably use the black inverted color only when I’m reading outside in bright sunlight.

I also am really happy to have buttons to turn the page again. It’s the ultimate laziness to be able to just keep your thumb in the button and depress it to turn the page instead of having to actually move your thumb a half inch to touch the screen, but hey, why move a half inch when your can push down 1/16th of an inch? All that extra movement add up over the years.
The real reason I like the buttons is this: I live in Alaska and we have very long, cold nights. But even in the winter, we turn down the heat at night. I read in bed every single night, tucked all cozy and warm under my down comforter... except for having to have my hand out in order to touch the screen on my Paperwhite to turn the page. My hand starts to get very cold. It’s uncomfortable. My half frozen hand takes away from my happy bedtime reading experience. With the Oasis, I can keep my hand under the blankets and just push the button. You don’t know what a big deal this is until you spend night after night with a frozen hand.

I also like that you can select which button to the the page advance button and which is the page back button. The Oasis comes set up with the top button as the page advance and the bottom as the page back, but I switched them: the bottom is the advance, the top is the back. I hold my ereaders at the bottom sides, and had to stretch my thumb to advance the page when it was set for the top button. It’s just easier and more comfortable to use the bottom button. And this is cool: the bottom button stays as my page advance button even when I rotate the Oasis 180 to use left handed!! Smart!!

Others have covered the size and weight so I won’t go it I all that except to say it’s comfortable to hold. I do use the official Amazon Premium leather cover and it fits perfectly, and the magnetic closure/sleep/wake functions work perfectly also.

Dislike: Nothing with the ereader itself, but with however Amazon picks the “special offers”. From what I read, these offers are supposed to be tailored off of a person’s reading history/preferences. I may be wrong.
The books they are featuring for me are “romance” genre. I am sooo not a romance genre girl. I don’t believe I’ve ever purchased this genre in my life. I’m a hardcore sci-fi/dystopian. I have an adverse reaction when I see romance special offer.

Other than that, some of the complaints by others leaves me wondering.
I just don’t think it’s THAT big of deal that it has a micro usb. Really, it’s just not that hard to figure out the big end of the cable from the small end. As for charging speed, charge mine while I’m sleeping at night so it doesn’t matter if it takes 1 hour or 4. I suppose having to carry a micro usb cord and charger when other devices use a usb-c cord/charger may be annoying but I think I can find 2 square inches in my purse/pocket/bag/backpack for it.

Also remember that this is an e-reader. It’s not a tablet, computer or smartphone, nor does it make any claims to be. Expecting an ereader to function basically like a computer/tablet/smartphone is expecting too much. It does an outstanding job at doing it’s job as an ereader.

I have sent many different type of files to my Paperwhite using my kindle email address and it’s worked excellent with that old ereader, so I expect this new Oasis will do excellent with those as well.

My suggestion is to read the description fully and know what you are getting and what you aren’t.
If your reading experience will be destroyed because this doesn’t have (nor claim to have) a usb-c, then this isn’t the ereader for you.
If you want it to be like a tablet or smartphone or computer, this isn’t the ereader for you.

But if you love reading and buy this for what it’s made for, I can recommend it.
Definitely look into getting a discount by trading in any unused kindles, and take advantage of the free Kindle Unlimited and Audible while they are available to offset the cost even more.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal)

UGREEN Lightning to USB Cable Data Syncing Charging Cord Compatible for iPhone 7,7plus,6S,6 Plus,iPhone5s,5c,5,iPad Mini,Mini 2,Air Etc MFI Certified (5ft, Silver) I have only recently started using UGREEN cables and so far every one of their cables I have used has been a top-notch product. I was interested to see how well their lightning cable would work out for me and, based on my experiences with their other cables I expected this cable to be excellent. I have not been disappointed.

First things first – this is an Apple-certified cable which is not insignificant. Because it is certified it will work right with your Apple device and the device will not complain about it being an unrecognized cable. If you have used cheaper cables that do not come with a certification you have seen the warning messages that appear when you connect it. This one will not cause that problem which is good right out of the box.

This cable seems to be well made and so far I have found no issues with build quality or assembly. The insulation is nice and thick and it securely attached on both ends so it will not pull away from the plugs. Each plug is shielded in an aluminum sheath which protects the plug and makes it a little easier to grip. I have the 5’ version of this cable which is nice; I like that I have a little more leeway with the extra length of the cable.

There’s something I want to emphasize about this cable which many might not consider or may think is insignificant. UGREEN has put their name right on the plug ends, where it is easy to see and read. This says that they believe in this product enough to brand it, which is actually uncommon. Most of the cables on my desk are not branded so it is very nice being able to identify a cable by manufacturer. When one goes bad, if it is not branded it is difficult to know where that cable came from. The very best micro USB cable I own is by UGREEN and because it is branded it is very easy for me to identify in the tangle on my desk. Now I can tell which lightning cable is theirs too.

I have not had this cable long enough to see how well it will hold up over time but in the time I have had it, it has been reliable and compatible. I like the extra length too which gives me some flexibility when figuring out where to put it and the device I connect to it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: UGREEN Lightning to USB Cable Data Syncing Charging Cord Compatible for iPhone 7,7plus,6S,6 Plus,iPhone5s,5c,5,iPad Mini,Mini 2,Air Etc MFI Certified (5ft, Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Z623 400 Watt Home Speaker System, 2.1 Speaker System - Black Latest edit after some frustrating months of use.

I ordered this as a TV speaker. That was in the description.
With no remote, and no way to raise or lower the sound without getting up, the item is useless to me. I like to watch TV in bed.
Who wants to keep getting up. As a computer speaker, it takes up a lot of space.very dissapointed.
I will donate it a church, where they will appreciate a loud speaker for youth groups.

Edit after 5 days use.

There is no remote. The volume is controlled by a dial. When using this connected to your TV, it's a major disadvantage getting up every time you need to change the volume. I have to downgrade from 5 stars to 4, because of this. They need to add to either a remote, or an app letting your phone control the volume. Not a problem when using this as a computer speaker, since the control is by your hand, not across the room. This is promoted as a TV speaker, not just a computer speaker, so it's a major fault.

Original review below.

I have been using the Logitech Z2300 that I purchased years ago. Connected to my computer and much appreciated when I listen to my apple subscription music. A real monster for a computer speaker. Thankfully, the Z 625 is decidedly smaller and fits on the bottom shelf of my 42 inch wood TV table with room to spare. There is also room left for my Amazon Echo and Braven wireless bluetooth speakers. The smaller size results in a much cleaner, more attractive package.

The dialog is much clearer than I expected. I have a ZVOX 450 on my main TV, so I do appreciate clear dialog.
I was disappointed that there is no bluetooth. The computer and Man Cave TV are on opposite sides of the same room, and having the Z2300 for music, and the Z625 for the TV is a bit too much. However, the problem was easily solved. On the Z625, I'm using the optical cable for the TV sound, and am using the enclosed jack to connect the speaker to my extra Iphone. As I type, I'm listening to Herman's Hermits through my Iphone to Z625 jack connection. The music is very soothing and suits my needs perfectly. No adjustments are needed when switching from the music through my smartphone via jack, or the TV sound through the optical cable. Automatic switching,

My TV test via optical was the opening of Game of Thrones. The subwoofer bass sounded great and added greatly to the enjoyment of watching the series. The galloping horses sounded thunderous.

Other considerations. I gave away my monstrous Polk system when we moved to our condo. Soundbars provide the cleanest look but really don't have any bass. My wife is picky. The soundbar is on the main TV for a cleaner appearance, while the Man Cave is a perfect home for this unit.

There was absolutely no documentation/instructions in the box, other than safety information. However hookup instructions were printed on the cardboard box. Don't destroy them opening it. Hooking up via optical was very intuitive and took minutes. I'd still like some instructions. For example, the power button is a push button. Does it shut off after inactivity? I'm doing it manually. Going by the Z2300, it probably won't make any difference. These are built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Z623 400 Watt Home Speaker System, 2.1 Speaker System - Black

StarTech.com StarTech.com 1-Port 10/100 Mbps Parallel Network Print Server - Fast Centronics Ethernet Printer Server Adapter - Windows 10 (PM1115P2) Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!

The design provides a stable center of gravity that allows it to securely hold devices up to 10" size in vertical or horizontal mode. I tested it with my iPad 4, a Kindle Fire HD, and an iPhone and found they all securely fit into the groove with or without cases on.

I can set it up on my desk or a table, run the power cord through the opening in the base and out through the back to charge it, and slide a Bluetooth keyboard over the stand's base. I also like experimenting with recipes I find online when I cook and I like being able to see the recipe better when it's on this stand. It's also very useful to get my iPad up off the counter in case I spill something too.

More and more schools assign homework that requires an iPad or other device, so this stand is very useful for studying. It's lightweight enough to move around effortlessly, but doesn't fold up flat so it is not convenient to take when traveling. This is a very well made stand that useful and convenient for home, school, or office use though, so I'd gladly recommend it for those uses.

It's not excessively far but it's out of range for a bluetooth device reach. It rings if anything goes through the circle (where the Camaro is) or down the drive past the house. I have tested it by walking at the very edge of the drive & it hasn't failed to alert. I may adjust the settings down before I move the receiver inside because it picks up a lot of cat activity. I didn't realize how many neighborhood cats stroll through my drive early in the morning.
I wanted to check this out before I committed to a mounting place so I set it under that oak tree. I thought it might be too shady to maintain the solar power requirements but it's been there a week with no issues. It's so discrete I'll probably just keep it on the rocks & move it closer to the tree. The mounting hardware is pretty nice, though, with a ball-jointed mount that sets up easy since it comes apart & has a lot of adjustment.
The receiver has three or 4 chimes & none of them are subtle. It also has another 30 or so songs. Some are holiday themed which could be fun if you were expecting guests for a party. It has some public domain tunes from the Baroque & Renaissance period as well as some contemporary tunes like "Music Box Dancer". I currently have it on what sounds like a mariachi band playing "March of the Toreadors" from Carmen which is kind of hilarious but I can't imagine what maniac would want to be alerted by that in their house ever. Most of the rest of the songs are like that.

text_fidelity_a: Dericam PTZ WiFi IP Security Camera,1080P Surveillance CCTV Outdoor Camera, Pan/Tilt/Zoom, 4X Optical Zoom, Night Vision, Motion Detection, IP65Weatherproof Pre-Installed 32G SD Card, Black I got two outdoor security cameras of different brands at the same time.  The other brand I could not get to work and setting it up was complicated and could apparently only be done through a cell phone.  This camera, on the other hand, could be set up with a computer and the setup was easy and I had it working within minutes, for a live feed.  The picture quality is good and I tested in the dark and still got a great picture.  I didn't give it 5 stars because I couldn't get it to record (supposedly it has some built-in memory, although you can also add a memory card for more memory).  For ease of setup and for the live feed, I give it 5 stars.  I'll try to work with it some more and if I get all the features working, will update this review.  Important note:  I got this without giving thought to the fact that I didn't have a good place to mount it outside.  Also, it needs an outlet to be plugged into, as do most security cameras.  I have outside outlets, but nothing up near the roof where I would want to mount this.  The power cord is not long enough to go for a very great distance, so might require an extension cord to run it.  An exposed extension to a security camera is not very secure, as all anyone would need to do is unplug it to disable the camera.  I thought perhaps I could just keep it inside and aim it out of a window.  Unfortunately my windows sills are two narrow for the camera to sit and shoot out of a window.  I didn't find a good way yet to mount in front of a windows.  Of course my lack of planning is no fault of the camera.  The camera seems rugged and well built.  It appears to be able to use 5Ghz Wi-Fi; the other camera I tested did not.  There is one slight design flaw; the aerial is very close to the mounting bracket, so it is difficult to position it properly.

text_fidelity_a:
Gosky Skyhawk 10x50 Monocular Scope - High Definition Fog- Proof Shockproof Monocular Telescope -Bak4 Prism FMC Monoscope for Bird Watching Hunting Camping Travelling Wildlife Secenery I don't know exactly where this would fit into a birders toolkit. For me, I am planning on taking it to the tropics with the kids as a cheap and easy to carry spotting scope. I'm hoping that I can remove the camera and set this up on the tripod with a quick release plate and put it on non moving birds and sloths etcetera so they don't get too frustrated with their bins. And I don't break my back with both camera and full spotting scope.

I will say this, in the 90's I paid $49 for a Russian surplus spotting scope that did have 20x zoom, but in every other way it was far, far inferior to this monocular. This has the passable optics for a beginning birder still not looking to invest well. It is fairly sharp in the center of the image but less so at the edges. It has a very small depth of field, but a surprising close focus of 6-8 feet. I would not recommend this as a replacement for a full set of bins, but you are getting half a budget pair binoculars.

The focus is easy enough to adjust one handed and it seems fairly well constructed in the hand. I would not want to drop it and fully test it, but it seems sturdy enough. Lense covers are also fine. The eye cup raises and lowers for eyeglass wearers but the mechanism seems less quality than other aspects of the monocular. I question the focal length placement for the cup at full or minimum extension. It seems like the missed the proper marks.

I think it will work for what I was hoping for, a rainforest spotting aid and a reserve optics for the car, but not sure I would recommend for much else.
text_fidelity_b: Gosky Skyhawk 10x50 Monocular Scope - High Definition Fog- Proof Shockproof Monocular Telescope -Bak4 Prism FMC Monoscope for Bird Watching Hunting Camping Travelling Wildlife Secenery

text_fidelity_a:
Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook This is one of those "why didn't I think of it?" type products. At first glance, it seems quite simple - basically a mini tripod with attachments that allow you to mount a tablet or phone. But after working with it for a while, it's clear a lot of thought went into this.

The tripod is well made and sturdy, consisting mainly of metal. The ball joint at the top is controlled by a built-in key that allows you to loosen and tighten it so it stays put. Each leg extends independently, so you can set the tripod so it is tilted upward (for example, to position a tablet so you can watch a movie at your desk). The attachment screw base has a rubber non-slip insert to protect whatever you're attaching against scratches. It includes a lanyard, but you can easily remove it (which I did) if it's not needed.

The tripod is very compact -- folds up to about 4.5 inches long and about 1 inch wide, so it's easy to carry. With the legs fully extended it is just under 9 inches tall. The legs have a thick rubber tip that keep it well balanced and positioned. I was a bit concerned that the legs didn't have locks, but the tension of the pull out extensions was more than adequate to keep the legs extended even when it was loaded down with an 8.9 inch Kindle Fire.

Impressive quality given the price - much better than expected.

You can also use the tripod as a camera tripod since the attachment screw is a standard size. It worked fine with my Panasonic and Canon point and shoots.

But the star of the show is the clip. You attach it to the back of the device case (you could attach it to the device itself, but it's not recommended) using an adhesive pad. The pad is removable, but is not reusable, so you want to give some thought before you stick it to the case. Once attached, it fits into a "smart mount" that, in turn, attaches to the tripod. Sounds kind of complicated, but it's very simple to use. There is an included instruction sheet, but you can pretty much puzzle it out by just looking at it.

The clip and smart mount are plastic, but seem more than sturdy enough for the job. They clip together with an interlocking system that kept my Kindle very solidly positioned while I was using it.

The only negative I see is the adhesive pad. As with any adhesive, you need to clean the point of contact very well (an alcohol pad is included in the box) and let the adhesive cure for 30 min. I think it's a safe bet that some people won't do both those steps, which opens the door to a significant point of failure.

But, provided you read the instructions, this is a very nicely designed and useful product. Highly recommend.
[The manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook

Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding I bought this at another website thanks to a Christmas gift card, but I researched the different types of sound bars and enhancement systems on Amazon & various places first. I wanted a very simple to use, unobtrusive setup, a digital connection and something that could work with our very open and large room without requiring setting up ugly components everywhere and still sound clean. This Denon base ticks every box for me.

I literally had this unit out of the box, installed under our 50" television, connected and working in less than 20 minutes - that includes reading the directions and unpacking. The box looked huge at first just sitting there alone, but once the tv was on top of it, it sort of vanished. Another 5 minutes and I had the Denon machine trained to respond to the volume buttons on my cable remote control. Mine came with a remote control, the digital optical cable and the red & white style connection. It connected to my phone and tablet via Bluetooth on the first try and played music through both using the Amazon Prime streaming and music saved to my devices - the sound is excellent by the way.

The included remote is handy for switching between daytime and night modes - the overall sound is lower in night mode. And you can choose between the surround sound mode or regular with the remote as well. One thing I have noticed, is that it can take three to five seconds for those changes to register and to hear them. The box turns on automatically when it senses a signal - no need to fiddle with it. Just turn the tv on & go about your business like always. The most impressive thing here is the improvement in the quality of the sound - every single bit is better! The guy reporting the news, music channels, background sound effects in movies, conversations in dramas... it's all crisp and clear and full. I am really pleased.

The two compare very favorably, and this TrendNet adapter may actually be a little faster.

Certainly this TrendNet adapter (the USB external, or dongle, version) is much easier to install! All that’s required is (1) to install the driver from the included CDROM (or to download the driver from the TrendNet web site); and (2) to plug the assembled adapter into a USB 3.0 port. Mine works fine when plugged into a USB 3.0 hub.

Assembling the adapter requires only that you screw the four antennae onto the base, and plug the USB 3.0 cable into the base.

For ease of installation and performance, it’s hard to beat this adapter. It makes the most of the high-speed Internet connection that I have from Comcast.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black For the simple fact that this camera can do EVERYTHING I want it to do in my pocket, it get 5+ stars. I could go on for days about this camera, but I will try to hold this review to my personal game-changers.

HFR: Shooting video at 1080p, 120fps (100MB) and slowing down the footage in post produces better slow-mo videos compared to the HFR feature that can do 1080p 240fps at the best quality. The ultra HFR feature was a big sell for me, but I feel like 480fps and 960fps have garbage quality and it's really really difficult to get the timing right when you are taking the shot in that feature mode because you only have a 2 second timeframe. I must have spent 2 hours trying to get a slow-mo shot of a bee in my garden when I first bought it, but could never get the timing right on pressing record when the stupid bee would start flying. Shooting in normal video mode at 120fps and slowing down in post at 24fps is seriously amazing, and I will likely never use the HFR again.

Time-Lapse: Pay the $9.99 extra to download this app, because holy cow, it is freaking awesome. There is full manual control over intervals, # shots, etc, and it blows me away that it can produce day-night time-lapse with little to no flicker and amazing color with accurate white balance throughout. If you don't want the hassle of editing the stills in post, then you can just have the camera produce a 1080p 24fps video file in-camera, although post allows you more creativity and ability to produce 4k time lapse.
Slog2: I've been shooting all my videos in Slog2 (4k & 1080p) since I bought the camera several months ago, and up until just now I did not have a computer beefy enough to process the footage in post (which is the reason I have waited on posting my review). For the last week, I've been color grading my Slog2 footage with the Color Finale plugin in Final Cut Pro X. The footage is stunning and the dynamic range blows me away. I'm still trying to figure out the over exposure sweet spot of shooting in Slog2, but for the most part it looks really nice when shot at +1 - +2 stops over exposed and re-adjusted in post. There's not as much noise in the shadows as I expected, and I'm about to get the Neat Video Noise Reduction plugin that I expect to help with the little noise that I'm seeing. I went out to Joshua Tree for the meteor shower and shot 4k 24fps video of the stars, which is insane for a little camera like this.

Lens: Having the faster lens fully zoomed in (f2.8) compared to the RX100 M1's f4.9 is changed the way I take photos of my baby. It really was difficult to get a decent bokeh shooting at typical portrait focal lengths with the M1, but very easy now with the M4. Fast, clean and crisp, this lens is great.

Compact Size: I wanted a camera that I can put in my pocket. As long as you don't wear skinny jeans, then you're good to go. I don't wear skinny jeans, but I'm just saying. Cargos are the best, but then I realize that I've become the dad that wears cargos, and then I see the guy in Honduras swapping heavy lenses with a dslr around his neck and don't feel so bad. Although, I often worry when it's in my pocket that the lens ring control might bend and not be as smooth as it is, but that hasn't happened.

Focus Modes: Changing between focus modes is my one gripe about this camera. In a run and gun environment, I have not been able to figure out how to easily toggle between the various auto focus modes. It's easy to go between MF and AF, but trying to toggle between the AF modes when trying to get the right video clip of my active baby is extremely difficult. However, note that using the lens ring in AF mode for rack focusing is possible, which I wasn't able to do on the RX100 M1.

Overall, I wanted a camera that could do EVERYTHING, do everything WELL, and that EVERYTHING it does WELL could fit in my pocket….
text_fidelity_b: Sony RX100 IV 20.1 MP Premium Compact Digital Camera w/ 1-inch Sensor, 4K Movies and 40x Super Slow Motion HD DSCRX100M4/B Black

text_fidelity_a: Optiarc AD-5290S-PLUS 24X SATA Internal DVD Optical Drives Burner with 8.7GB Overburn for XGD3 Support (Black) In order to try the over burn feature, I would need the appropriate disks that can normally hold 8.5 GB (DVD+R).  These disks are not too difficult to find online, but the office supply stores only seem to stock 4.7 GB disks.  I guess you either have to special order or buy online.  Most everything that I need to burn can either fit on a 4.7 GB DVD or can be compressed (without much loss of quality) to fit.  It may be false economy to buy the higher capacity disks, as they are nearly double the price of lower capacity.  With burnable media prices being so low anyway, you don't gain much by squeezing as much as you can on a particular disk.  So why did I get this drive?  I like to have a drive on the shelf if one goes bad (and they do sometimes), and then I don't have to wait for one to arrive.  I assumed it was probably good to have one that can burn to maximum capacity as this isn't much more expensive than a regular DVD burner.  Since I haven't actually installed or used the drive yet (waiting for disks), one should not pay as much attention to my review as some other reviewers.  I just wanted people to be aware that you can't insert a 4.7 GB disk and expect to over burn to 8.7 GB.  You need to understand the differences in available media and get the appropriate blank media. Update:  I finally received the appropriate media to test the drive.  It seemed to work good for the first 6 or 8 disks, but then 3 disks in a row had burn errors.  Bad media?  I don't think so; it appears the drive is failing already.  I'll test on another computer and see if it is the media or the drive and update the review again, but right now I can't recommend this drive at all.  UPDATE 2:  I tried this again after rebooting my computer and it now seems to work fine and does indeed overburn, so you can squeeze a lot on one disk.  When I had 3 bad burns in a row, I thought it was the burner, but it may have been bad media.  On the other hand, I suspect something flaky on my PC, as I have had bad burns before occasionally (not recently) and then after a reboot everything was fine again.  I may have too many programs loaded when I try to burn.  That's not the fault of the DVD drive.  Most likely the fault of the burning program (and I am using a major well-know program.)
text_fidelity_b: Optiarc AD-5290S-PLUS 24X SATA Internal DVD Optical Drives Burner with 8.7GB Overburn for XGD3 Support (Black)

SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM I haven't bothered with a video camera in many years - using an excellent cell phone camera is just so much easier and convienent. That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.
text_fidelity_b: SOSUN Video Camera Camcorder HD 1080P 24.0MP 3.0 Inch LCD 270 Degrees Rotatable Screen 16X Digital Zoom Camera Recorder and 2 Batteries(301S-Plus), 301AM

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 265/265T 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Traffic I previously owned a Garmin Nuvi 360 which I loved. I specifically need a GPS that includes Bluetooth, since I use it both for directions and for hands-free phone use (which is rare, but important when I need it). I loved my 360 and used it daily until just a few months ago, when the Bluetooth suddenly stopped working. After troubleshooting with Garmin's tech support, it was determined the unit would need to be sent in for service, and since it was out of warranty, the flat charge for service was $79, which didn't include insured shipping costs.

Well, do the math. Obviously, one can acquire a brand-new GPS for not much more than $79, so I started shopping. That's how I ended up with my new Garmin Nuvi 265T. And I LOVE IT! I'm almost glad that my old unit went on the fritz, because it gave me an excuse to upgrade to this newer, fantastic unit.

The 360 was great for accurate directions, easy to see and read display, and consistent Bluetooth (until it broke). Here's how the 265T is even better:

- Smaller, lighter, and thinner, but with a slightly wider screen.
- No "antenna" on the back to flip up and fiddle with - it just works.
- Uses my existing mount (from ProClips), so no change to that was necessary.
- Includes FREE traffic notifications, which so far seem to work pretty well.
- When you power it on, it seems to bypass the warning screen that you need to "Agree" to quicker, and then shows a simple display: Where To, and View Map. On the 360, if you didn't do anything else, it would sit on the menu indefinitely, but the 265T automatically switches to map display after a few minutes if you don't select anything else. Basically, you can start your car and just forget about it, until you need it!

The traffic feature is ad-supported, so occasionally very small banner-type ads appear on the display, usually offering coupons for local restaurants etc. They are quite small and not intrusive in any way, so I don't mind them. I guess there's also an option to upgrade to a paid traffic service that would not include ads, but I don't see a need for that for my own use.

In general I am thrilled with Garmin products, and this Nuvi 265T is no exception. What a great deal, and a nice early Christmas present for myself!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 265/265T 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Traffic

While my office offered to let me take my monitors home I just didn't have the space, and I do like to occasionally do work at the local cafe or lounge.

Enter this portable screen...

My only criticism would be that anytime it gets unplugged from the laptop, the settings reset, and when you plug it back in you have to readjust the settings. It's only 4 button presses to change it which I have down now so its not a big deal but it would be nice if this setting was memorized somehow.

In the days of COVID and WFH, this has been one of the best productivity purchases I've made and it has been beyond worthwhile.

text_fidelity_a:
FULLJA WiFi Digital Picture Frame - 10.1 Inch Smart Digital Photo Frame with FHD IPS Touch Screen, 32GB Memory, Motion Sensor WiFi Electronic Picture Frame Share Photos and Videos Via App Email I don’t love it. This seems overpriced for what you get. For the price, I was expecting it to look more like a photo frame but instead, it kinda feels like an old monitor. My goal was to hang it on the wall during art shows with process videos playing. It will work OK for that but I’m disappointed that unless the video is in the exact proportion of the frame, it will always look a little “off” and there’s no means of changing how it’s framed in the display.

I think it’s at its best without the clock or any other additions.

The pros: It really does work right out of the box. It only took minutes to get photos onto it. The big screen is nice, I can see details in my photos. It is also bright with vivid colors. I like that it is flat which is why it performs better than an average monitor as a picture frame. The simple black frame doesn’t detract from its appearance. I like that there is an app and my husband and I were able to add photos, and I also like that there is a way to add photos via card in case software changes make the app obsolete. With the app, I was able to get videos onto it in minutes. I also like that it has a large amount of storage space and the means to expand it..

The cons: It is slow. I didn’t love the way the photos are displayed. I also hate the default animations because they are a bit cheesy. I want it to fade or some other non-intrusive way to change photos, and there is no means to edit it. The features are incredibly barebones. I hate that the default includes the time etc, I just want it to look like a photo frame! The audio is a bit tinny, much more so than a television etc. I also find it bizarre in 2023 to have an item that warns that it can destroy a USB if it’s removed without turning it off first…that seems like such an old-school problem!

I wish the plug was white because the black looks bad against the wall, and I prefer a minimalist look.

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple) There's a lot to like about the Playsport. For one, it's very easy to use as a point and shoot should be. The picture quality is certainly fine for just about anybody's use, save for those who really like blowing their pictures up large. It's very fast to move between photos and movie--a few thumb moves is all it takes. The same for toggling between the movie quality. Which means if you suddenly want to grab a still photo while videoing or are worried about recording room and want to drop down a notch or two in quality, you can do so without missing a lot of action. The zoom is a 3X, which is serviceable. I'd prefer longer and I'm sure the next version will offer a longer zoom, but as I use this for quick shots of the family and not for event shooting, the 3X is rarely an issue in terms of not being adequate.

Transfer of files is easy and fast (I use a Mac) and all the cables come bundled with it. Yes, you read that right--it ships with all the needed cables.

Because it is so small and slim, and held in that vertical position, it can get a bit shaky and you'll need to pay attention to keeping it steady, more so than larger cameras or ones you hold with two hands horizontally. The sound pickup is fine save that wind noise can be a problem on windy days--it'll wash out a good deal of the speaking sound.

It feels rugged out of the box and the number of times I've dropped it, including just recently while chasing my boy and his friend around the corner of the house and getting my foot caught in the extension cord of the Halloween decorations. I watched the camera skid across several feet of concrete sidewalk but it was none the worse for wear.

It's slimness makes it a great pocket camera--one of those where it's defined as such not because you can cram it into your pocket and walk around like you have a grapefruit in there but where it slips right in and you barely notice it. That's one of the reasons it's become the camera I take most often when I know I won't need a larger zoom or a flash.

I haven't tried the underwater aspect in actual underwater conditions (snorkeling, say), but a few practice photos in the pool shows it takes pretty sharp photos in that environment. But I'll leave the gauging of that aspect to those more well-versed in such a need.

In the end, it's a great little camera and as mentioned, it's quickly become the one I carry along most often when we're just heading out for some family fun. For post-dusk indoor, I take a Canon elph and for events or hiking a Canon IS with a 12x zoom and a tele-converter. But for playing games in the yard, birthday parties, classroom events, etc.--the Kodak has become the go-to camera.

highly recommended
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlaySport (Zx3) HD Waterproof Pocket Video Camera (Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000 Though I have a laptop, I decided to use this solid-state drive as a boot drive on my desktop computer. If you are unfamiliar with the difference between a solid-state and a regular hard drive, the solid-state has no moving parts, which makes it silent, fast, reliable, and shock resistant. It has twice the capacity and twice the speed of the solid-state drive I got a couple of years ago for the same price, and blows away a standard drive for speed.

Given the silence and speed, it makes a great boot drive for running Windows, Photoshop, and other programs where speed is a huge advantage. Just to give you an idea, when upgrading from a regular two-year-old hard drive to this solid-state drive, my Windows boot time went from two minutes to about 10 seconds. Seriously, my computer now starts up and is ready to use in like 10 seconds.

What I do is use a solid-state drive as my boot drive and a regular hard drive as a storage drive. Solid-state drives like this are really expensive to purchase if you need any kind of capacity, but a 200 GB drive will certainly hold all of your programs and often used files.

As for this drive specifically, I hooked it up to my desktop and it was immediately recognized by Windows. The drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up as a drive and work in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

As I said, it's a lot faster than the solid-state drive I had from a couple years ago, and there's no problem using it on my desktop machine rather than my laptop.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000

Young and broke, I saved and finally got a used triangle phone. By the way, in the movie 'The Birdcage', the receptionist is using one of the Bang & Olufsen banana phones. B&Os are in a lot of films.
Why?

In my most humble opinion, Bang & Olufsen is at the top of the game when it comes to visual design. Over the years they have always shown products that are visually stunning, MOMA worthy.

This headset is no different.
It is true understated elegance.
The two shades of grey are exactly the 'right' shades. We all know what that means, it's like the difference between and on trend pleasing pink, and a Pepto-Bismol pink. The spun metallic is in a warm tone gives a more inviting feel to the set.
Easy to sync.
I do not expect these to sound like a $1,000 headset, if they were, I'd be slightly underwhelmed. But only slightly.
As far as dimension, the 3d effect, it's spectacular. The band or orchestra is right in front of you.
They pick up the nuance that other headphones miss. Funny story, I was listening to a song I've listened to a hundred times before, and heard some background that I had never heard before.

Just a heads up for those of us that wear red nail polish... I've taken these on and off so many times that little red streaks are starting to appear, as you can see in the photo. But you can also see how gorgeous these are.

It won't turn on sometimes, or it will take 30 seconds to power up, or other variations. I wish that I had known about these issues before I purchased this TV because I might have looked at different manufacturers..

Called the 800 number found out that manufacturer warranty is gone obviously. No offers of a free diagnostic or anything like that. They did provide a local number for technition but with it being a weekend chances are no one is there. I am going to see if there is anything I can visually pick up in the power supply and do some basic testing. Will do another update after this is resolved one way or another

I've tried various different types. Some that are "truly wireless", some like these that have the connected wire around the neck. These Jabra Evolve 65e earbuds are really pretty amazing for what they are. Sound is great but not booming with bass. They are crisp yet not loud. There is really no sound isolation as the buds don't fit snug in the ear, (even trying the included different size tips and wings) but that seems to be on purpose. As from I can tell from reading about these, is that they are meant to allow some outside sound, so that if you are say jogging, you should be able to hear to be safe right? Now with that said, I see the purpose and the market for these earbuds, and there is absolute value to these.
Pairing these to my Android mobile phone was an absolute breeze. Also, using the USB Bluetooth adapter on my Chromebook made pairing these super simple as well.
Call quality is on par with most wireless earbuds. It's good, but not the same as just using your phone obviously but better than some "cheap" buds I've tried. These are definitely built with the Jabra quality you would expect and I'm overall impressed.
They fit comfortably and secure and I've had no issue with them popping out, but then again I'm not a jogger. They are easy to fit into your ears, unlike others that I've had that take a bit of twisting to get the fit just right.
The app is nice and works well but as with most apps like this, it's gimmicky. I mean I've played with it a bit at first but any more, I just pop the buds in and go, and haven't used the app in quite a while.
So to summarize, these are great earbuds if you don't need "truly wireless" and you don't need sound isolation.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 65e Wireless Neckband Headset, Link 370, MS-Optimized – Bluetooth Headset with up to 13 Hours of Battery Life – Superior Sound for Calls and Music – Passive Noise Cancelling Headset

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa I'm not a gamer, but I do have around 30 devices connected to a home network. These include WEMO switches, Amazon Echos, a smart TV, a playstation, Kindles, iPads, printers, and smartphones. The "dynamic Quality of Service" feature of this NIGHTHAWK X4 ULTIMATE GAMING ROUTER (R7500v2) seems to prioritize these devices, so that all of them are more responsive (faster connections) than they were with my previous router (a rock-solid NIGHTHAWK (R7000)).

When this NIGHTHAWK (R7500v2) is set up, it recognizes all of the "Internet of things" devices for what they are. In the "attached devices" list, these aren't given device names (e.g., "iPad", picked up from the device itself) but have "n/a" in the name column (and you can't assign them names even if you know them by the MAC numbers). I don't know exactly how the "Quality of Service" feature performs its magic, but now when I ask an Amazon Echo to turn on a light or a fan, the Echo performs the task immediately--instead of with a delay while it searched through the router's list of connected devices for the correct one.

The PCs and other devices that use lots of bandwidth (instead of being on standby much of the time) seem to connect faster, and they test (using OOKLA) at significantly faster Internet speeds.

My R7500v2 is broadcasting signals for both bands (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), and my compatible devices connect with the 5 GHz network whenever I ask them to. However, I don't use the 5 GHz band for anything at present (because it's easiest to have everything that uses a printer on the same band with the printers). Thus I don't know whether the router frequently drops the 5 GHz signal, as other reviewers have stated.

I've used several high-end Linksys routers, and they have performed very well. However, I find that Netgear routers lose their Internet signal far less often, and almost never require rebooting--when Netgear routers need rebooting, the issue is almost always traceable to Comcast problems.

Another reason that I prefer Netgear routers over Linksys routers is that Netgear has no limit (or a very high limit) on the number of devices that you can list by MAC number and tell the router to "allow only these devices to connect to the network". I use this feature as an extra firewall, and find that the Linksys 25-device list is inadequate for my needs.

Finally, the Netgear "Genie" app for managing the router settings is clear and easy to understand. The initial setup for this router is easy, unless you have a nonstandard home network (e.g., my router is connected with the Comcast-supplied equipment in "Bridge" mode), and/or you interrupt the setup routine before it's run through all its steps. If you do land in setup limbo, you can start over by resetting the router to the factory settings (use a paperclip to hold down the reset button for 10-30 seconds--light will blink; unplug from wall for 30 seconds; follow Quick Start instructions again from beginning).
text_fidelity_b: Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa

One day it just stopped charging. I had read dozens of books on there, and had the wifi plus 3g version which was very convenient.

I occasionally read now on the Kindle app on my computer, as I have about 97 books in my library, with probably 15-20 still unread. I noticed on Amazon that there was a promotion...Kindles on sale for Prime members. I thought, you know, it would be nice to read those books I've put off reading because it's just not the same on my computer or phone...I think I'll get another Kindle. I researched reviews for a little while, and decided all I needed was the Paperwhite with Wi-fi. The additional cost for 3G was just not worth it to me...sure, I'd used it before when traveling with my old Kindle to buy a few books, but with a little planning I could've purchased and downloaded the books beforehand. Also, some of the reviews of the higher end Kindles did not impress me.

Anyway, I received the Kindle earlier today. It came almost fully charged, and was so easy to set up. And within minutes had books from my Kindle library loaded! I've been reading for 2 hours straight and so far I love it. I am using it on maximum brightness, sure it may take more frequent charging, but I really love how bright it is and the contrast of the words on the page. I also bought a cover for it and find it is easier to hold IMO. Pages turned with a simple finger swipe.

Hopefully this will last a very long time! I've got so many books I want to read!

Couple this with the fact that people no longer want to develop photos, they merely rely on cell phones to post, instagram, or tweet. But for those who are “old school” and want something tangible to send hold or send, the Fuji Instax Mini 26 is perfect.

This small camera is: (1) easy to hold; (2) easy to use; (3) affordable, the camera -under $70; the film – under $20 depending on the pack you select; (4) it’s lightweight/portable; and (5) MORE IMPORTANTLY, CUTE (it comes in a variety of colors).

Now I have some suggestions about what can you do with this small camera: Let me give you a few options: (1) You can capture candid moments at a wedding. Just imagine all of the moments you will capture if you place one of these delightful gems on each table, at the reception. This is the perfect opportunity to capture those candid shots and moments of your guest, ones that will probably not be captured by a wedding photographer. You could then create a pin board for guest to post photos and make comments, or use the photos for a scrapbook. (2) You could make your own Photo Booth for graduation parties, birthday parties - Sweet 16 Birthday Party, Football tailgating parties; etc, without having to print out tons of photos. Again capturing all of those moments that you normally wouldn’t get but that you can cherish for a lifetime. (3) This is a perfect gift. Young teens or kids can use this camera to do school projects, selfies or just have fun.

Overall, while this camera will not appeal to “real” photographers, I think there is a real market for people who want to have fun. However, not that while this camera is fun, it is a tad bit pricey. I highly recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this as a graduation present for my nephew and, of course, had to try it out for a while just to make sure it was "in proper functioning order." (OK, so I like toys even more than the kids do).

Very nice system! It's a nice improvement from earlier Nuvi's I've used. Love the improved software, especially the full-time next-turn indicator (long a favorite feature of mine on Magellan units). The screen layout is attractive and easy to use, even for those of us with less than perfect eyesight.

While I personally like the Magellan systems better for my own use, I picked this for the nephew for a couple of reasons. First, it has features such as the ability to download Google maps directions. Not something I would use, but a nice feature for those who would use it. Second, it has the ability to display the speed limit. While it won't prevent speeding, at least it's a reminder for a younger driver to keep it slow.

I found the routing engine to be top-notch. Every GPS does that a bit different, but every route I planned on it was plotted out in a logical manner. It's a bit slower to detect off-route conditions and re-route compared with Magellans, but certainly does it at an acceptable speed. Boot up and acquitiion time is very good, as it the overall build quality and form factor.

A good option to pick up is a bean bag mount such as a NavMat. Makes it far easier to hide the GPS without any trace to tip off potential theves.

Most important, it has Garmin support - they are far better than Magellan, and can be used as a resource for someone who is using their first GPS. I was sorry to have to hand it back over the the nephew, but he's thrilled with it!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255W 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa, 10.1" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I love everything else Amazon has ever done, so it breaks my heart to write this review. I've had a couple of iPads and they work great, but I find Apple's pricing and politics ridiculous, so I was excited to move away from them and go with an Amazon product. Sadly, the Fire HD is seriously inferior.

This device is SLOW. Every step of the setup process was painfully slow. Downloading, and even opening, apps is slow. I have my OLD iPad sitting right next to the Fire HD performing the same functions on the same WiFi connection and the Fire takes 4 times as long to do anything.

The WiFi connectivity is not great. Again, I have my old iPad 3 sitting right next to this device, and the Fire HD keeps losing the network connection or dropping down to 1-2 bars, while the iPad is streaming and loading everything with lightning speed. Funny thing is, I have a Fire TV Stick running in the same room, and it has a wonderfully reliable, super-fast connection!

The touch screen is also sometimes not very responsive - I will have to tap some things 4-5 times before they trigger.

Most of the apps I was looking for are available in the Amazon App Store. However, these are buggy versions that appear to have been thrown together without the care that the developers have put into their iOs versions.

Possibly the worst part of all is the battery life. We are supposed to get 8 hours of usage.... I get about 4, even with the screen set as dim as possible. It also completely discharges on standby (with NO USE) within 2 days, even with the setting enabled to turn off WiFi when the device is on standby.

I do love the integration with the Amazon ecosystem. I hope someday Amazon will make the necessary improvements and I can give their tablets another chance. But for now, I will be returning this device with a heavy heart. :(
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa, 10.1" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

USB C to USB Hub 4 Ports, Siawclub USB 3.0 Hub with a Type C to USB Adapter, Thunderbolt 3 to USB Hub Compatible with Thunderbolt 4 MacBook Pro, Pad Pro, Mac, Surface, Grey I got this to carry with my laptop, which has just the two USB-A ports one of which has my mouse dongle. So clearly not enough sometimes. This is nice little adapter supporting USB3 speeds, and the compact size makes it particularly good to throw into the laptop bag. The A/C adapter is also handy since my work laptop has an available C port, but no open A port.

I tested this with large file transfers on my Windows 10 desktop, copying files from an SSD to a USB3 drive. I consistently got about 45MB/s (bytes, not bits), which is what I would expect for this kind of transfer -- and I confirmed that it's the same whether I use the hub or plug the drive in directly.

So if you're looking for a handy and versatile little 4-port USB3 hub, this one should be high on your shortlist.

text_fidelity_a:
THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen I have to agree that the way I need to mount it isn't the best the engineers could have come up with. Sticking it to my windshield makes it so I can't change the view. I mean NO flexibility at all. Some type of mount, similar to what Garmin uses, and attaching it to the dashboard would have been better. A big star taken off for this. I'll have to come up with something that's more useful than what this is.

Nothing complicated with setting this up. Just pop in the memory card, plug it into the charge port in vehicle, and that's it. Then connect it to your iOS or Android device through Wi-Fi to stream and download recordings. This is also how you configure the device to the settings you want.
What I can't find in any of the product details is the size of the memory card that came with it.
Memory Card that's in the box is 8 gb.

Wish the instructions gave more details on the camera use. But, it's really easy to search and find it online:
[...]
[...]

The viewing screen is a nice size. And I like that it notifies of upcoming traffic enforcement cameras.
Has nice video quality.

Cons:
Memory card could have been larger.
Don't like how it attaches to the windshield.
For the price, I wish it came with the optional accessories: External GPS Tracker and a Hardwiring Cable for Parking Surveillance Mode.
text_fidelity_b: THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen
